text:
marta: Heads-up — seeing a sharp p99 latency spike from HEL POP starting ~08:14 UTC. Kinda noisy: CPU steal and scheduler delays on 3 hosts. Logs + flamegraph attached.

devon: I can see oscillation in kernel selector decisions on those hosts. Kernel switch flapping every ~30s causing batch size changes and KV-cache pressure.

sam: Is this noisy neighbor (other tenant causing CPU contention) or something at the host/kernel level? Any io_wait spikes?

marta: Steal time is high (~18-22%), softirq elevated. iostat shows sporadic throughput bursts but not sustained IO saturation. Looks like CPU scheduler preemption to us.

li: Profiling hints: when kernel selector flips from kernel_v2 -> kernel_v1 we get batch-size drop from 64->8, so effective qps drops and request batching floods the KV cache leading to eviction churn.

anya: Got the flamegraphs. Primary hotspots: sched_migrate, kvm_vcpu_run (we're on metal with nested qemu?), and heavy futex syscalls from a background process (non-redwood) on those hosts.

infra-bot: deploy-event: autoscaler triggered rebalancing at 08:16:12 UTC for helsinki-pool-3 due to node pressure. No config changes.

devon: So chain: noisy process -> scheduler preemption -> kernel selector oscillates -> batch heuristic shrinks -> KV cache gets thrash -> p99 spikes. Makes sense.

sam: Any quick mitigation we can try? Throttle background tenants, isolate CPUs, or force kernel selector to stick to a conservative kernel variant.

li: We tested `isolcpus` on a warm host in canary yesterday; reduced steal and stopped the kernel selector flipping under load. But that requires host reboot / config push.

anya: Could we rate-limit batching at the runtime level as temporary fallback? For example cap to 16 tokens per batch in HEL region while we remediate.

marta: Ops suggested traffic steering: move HEL non-critical traffic to FRA POP for 30m. That would reduce load and let infra team patch hosts.

ops-bot: reroute: FRA fallback rule applied to helsinki-pop for routes: chat-generate-prod, embed-prod at 08:45 UTC.

devon: Also toggled `kernel_selector.disable_autoswitch=true` on one canary host at 08:50. Early result: selector stayed on kernel_v2 and batch sizes remained stable for 20m.

li: Collected perf traces pre/post toggle. Attaching `perf script` snippet:

```
# before toggle
[   0.000]   sched: scheduler_migrate  32.1%
[   0.000]   futex_wait              18.5%

# after toggle
[   0.000]   user_samples             60.2%
[   0.000]   kernel_samples           10.3%
```

marta: After reroute + disable_autoswitch, p99 fell from 1.2s -> 220ms across the affected routes. KV cache eviction rate dropped by 87%.

sam: Next actions: 1) Infra to identify noisy tenant process and noise source on the 3 hosts (Marta + Infra). 2) Gradually roll `disable_autoswitch` for all HEL runtime hosts as stopgap (Devon). 3) Plan permanent fix: cpuset/cgroup isolation + kernel knob tuned or change kernel selection heuristic to consider steal/softirq (Li).

anya: Also add a guard in batching heuristic: if selector oscillation detected, pin batch size to last-stable value and avoid aggressive downscaling for 60s.

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-5823 "HEL noisy-host scheduler/tenant causing kernel selector oscillation" assigned to infra-team, priority P1.

marta: I'll keep monitoring. Reopen thread if we see recurrence after rolling the stopgaps out. :thumbsup:

devon: Thanks — good triage. We'll follow up with postmortem including perf artifacts and a proposed kernel-selection change. :eyes:

ops-bot: incident-note: traffic steering rolled back at 09:30 UTC once hosts confirmed stable by infra.

marta: Final status: mitigation successful, ongoing follow-ups assigned.
